svg.title: Adding position
svg.desc: Why models need position, and how the original Transformer added it. First, without position, "dog bites man" and "man bites dog" contain the same three tokens, so attention alone gives the same result for both. Second, with position, every token is stamped with its place in the sentence, 0, 1 or 2, so "dog at position 0" and "dog at position 2" become different inputs: the input is the token vector plus a position vector. Third, the position vector comes from waves at different speeds. Four waves are drawn across positions 0 to 16, from the fastest to the slowest. Reading all four waves at position 5 gives that position its own stamp: about −0.96, +0.60, +0.89 and +0.43. Nearby positions get similar stamps.
svg.text: Attention ignores word order on its own, so each token gets a stamp that says where it sits.
1 · WITHOUT POSITION: A BAG OF WORDS
Attention compares every token with every other one, so it
sees the same set either way. It can't tell who bit whom.
2 · WITH POSITION: EVERY TOKEN GETS A STAMP
The same word now looks different at each position.
3 · THE POSITION VECTOR: WAVES AT DIFFERENT SPEEDS
Sinusoidal position encoding from the original Transformer (2017), shown for 4 of the d/2 pairs. Wave speeds are simplified for the drawing.
